newsitem.title: USA: Carter-Wallace off after rejecting Davis bid.
newsitem.headline: Carter-Wallace off after rejecting Davis bid.

text.p: Shares in Carter-Wallace Inc tumbled over 10 percent on Friday after it confirmed Wall Street expectations by rejecting a buyout bid.
"No surprise there," said one arbitrager after Carter-Wallace said its majority shareholder, CPI Development Corp, rejected a tender offer from investor Marvin Davis.
Davis on Wednesday offered to buy all outstanding shares for $18 per share.
Carter-Wallace was down 1-5/8 to 13-7/8 Friday afternoon. The stock rose 28 percent on Wednesday.
Davis spokesmen were not immediately available for comment on what the investor's next move would be after the Carter-Wallace rejection.
"The key thing is whether the bid is increased or there are other bids," said Salomon Brothers analyst Diana Temple. But she declined to speculate on those possibilities.
Carter-Wallace said that after its majority shareholder snubbed the $18 a share offer, it would take "no further action" on the Davis proposal.

With Carter-Wallace insiders controlling about 82 percent of the company via common stock and a special class of shares, Davis or any other potential bidder would have a hard row to hoe, another arbitrager said.

"I think (Davis) has got something up his sleeve but it's going to be an uphill battle," the arbitrager said. "It's going to have to be a real pretty bid for (Carter-Wallace owners) to give (the company) up."
Carter-Wallace is a health-care products company with brands including Trojan condoms and Arrid deodorant.
